units: <cite ref="Gittin 23b:12">Gitt. 23ᵇ</cite> <he>העבד … רַבּוֹ של חבירו אבל לא מיד רַבּוֹ שלו</he> a slave may receive a deed of manumission in behalf of a fellow slave at the hand of his fellow’s master, but not at the hands of his own master (if both slaves belong to the same master).

<cite ref="Berakhot 63b:8">Ber. 63ᵇ</cite> <he>יאמרו הרב בכעס וכ׳</he> they will say, the teacher (the Lord) is angry, and the disciple (Moses) is angry, what is to become of Israel? <cite ref="Berakhot 63b:24">Ib.</cite> <he>כל תלמיד … רבו וכ׳</he> a student with whom his teacher is angry for the first time, and who keeps silence.
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 1:16">Ab. I, 16</cite> <he>עשה לך רב וכ׳</he> get thyself a teacher, and be relieved of doubt.
<cite ref="Mishnah Rosh Hashanah 2:9">R. Hash. II, 9</cite> <he>רַבִּי ותלמידי רבי וכ׳</he> my teacher and my pupil; my teacher in wisdom &c.; v. <cite ref="T00085"><he>רַבִּי</he></cite>.—
M. Kat. 9ᵃ, a. fr. למדתנו רַבֵּינוּ thou, our teacher, hast taught us; v. רַבֵּנוּ; a. v. fr.—Esp. רַב Rab,
<cite ref="Pesachim 52b:11">Pes. 52ᵇ</cite>; a. v. fr.—<he>בי רב</he> the school of, v. <cite ref="B00536"><he>בֵּי</he></cite>.—
senses.label: a

senses.gloss: surname of Abba Arekha, the founder of the academy of Sura in Babylonia (v. Graetz, Gesch. d. Jud.<sup>1</sup> IV, p. 312, sq.; Fr. M’bo, p. 122ᵇ).
units: <cite ref="Chullin 95b:16">Ḥull. 95ᵇ</cite> <he>כולהו שני דרב וכ׳</he> as long as Rab lived, R. Joḥ. addressed his letters to Babylonia, ‘to our teacher in Babylonia.’ <cite ref="Avodah Zarah 10b:16">Ab. Zar. 10ᵇ</cite> <he>אדרכן שמשיה לרב</he> A. (a Parthian ruler) attended (associated with) Rab.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Peah 6:3:5">Y. Peah VI, 19ᶜ</cite> <he>רב כד נחת לתמן</he> when Rab came down to Babylonia.
<cite ref="Eruvin 50b:15">Erub. 50ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>רב תנא הוא ופליג</he> Rab is a Tannai and has a right to differ (with other Tannaim).

<cite ref="Niddah 24b:68">Nidd. 24ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>הלכתא כרב וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="A01407"><he>אִיסּוּרָא</he></cite>; a. v. fr.—<he>ספרא דבי רב</he>, <he>ספרי דבי רב</he>, v. <cite ref="O01426"><he>סִפְרָא</he></cite>.—Pl. <he>רַבּוֹת</he> (only with suffix).
<cite ref="Shevuot 47a:6">Shebu. 47ᵃ</cite> <he>רַבּוֹתֵינוּ שבבבל וכ׳</he> ‘our teachers in Babylonia’ means Rab and Samuel.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 7:3:2">Y. Gitt. VII, 48ᵈ</cite> top <he>ורבותינו אמרו</he> and our teachers said; <he>מנו רבותינו וכ׳</he> who are meant by ‘our teachers’? <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 7:3:2">Ib.</cite>, a. e. <he>בשלשה … רבותיני</he> on three occasions R. Judah (with his court) is quoted as ‘our teachers.’ <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 5:4:7">Y. Sabb. V, end, 7ᶜ</cite> <he>רבותינו שבגולה</he> our teachers in the diaspora (Babylonia, v. supra); <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Beitzah 2:5:4">Y. Bets. II, 61ᶜ</cite> bot.
Y. Meg. I, 70ᵈ כתבו אגרת ושלחו לרבותינו שהן וכ׳ they (Mordecai and Esther) wrote a letter addressed ‘to our teachers (in Palestine) that be’, saying to them &c.; a. fr.—Fem. רַבָּה mistress.
<cite ref="Ruth Rabbah 4:6">Ruth R. to II, 5</cite> <he>רַבָּתָהּ וכ׳</he> her mistress (Naomi) &c., v. <cite ref="T00931"><he>רָפָה</he></cite>.
